non-probabilistic.","The cost of error in physical testing is catastrophic failure, whereas in Popperian science the 'cost' is merely the loss of a hypothesis, which is viewed as a gain in guarantees future performance."],"source_memory_refs":["bridge_stress_test_protocol","chess_opening_selection_heuristic"],"transfer_claims":["Just as an engineer tests the bridge design that has the severity of the next test.","The preference is a rule of procedure (how to play the game of science) rather than a statement of fact (the state of the board)."]},"claim":"The preference for Miller).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Popper distinguishes between the logical status of a theory (which remains unproven and improbable) and the methodological decision of which theory to test next. Preferring the highly corroborated theory is a strategic choice because it has withstood severe tests, meaning it has high empirical content. By choosing it, we subject ourselves to the highest risk of refutation. If it fails, we learn more; if it survives, our knowledge grows. This avoids induction because we do not claim the past success predicts future success (probability); we only claim that testing the 'boldest' conjecture currently available is the most efficient engine for error elimination.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
